title: Eight and Oh, and Still Not Quite Believable
dek: Peyton stays perfect, Dustin hangs 126.4 on a team that scored 29.6, and Trey's playoff odds fall off a cliff.

sections.head: The lead
body: The Loose Stools are 8–0, and the standings say so loudly. The underlying numbers are quieter. Peyton put up the week's top score, 146.3, to beat Mike's 136.0. That made Mike the season's highest-scoring loser and kept Peyton the league's only unbeaten team. It also moved Peyton back to No. 1 in the power rankings.

Then there's the luck column. Peyton has scored like a 6.0-win team and owns eight wins, the biggest gap in the league, and his all-play record sits at .750, behind Connor & Kunal's .818. Nobody is giving the wins back, but if you're looking for the league's best team rather than its best record, it's still Got New Legs.

sections.head: Around the league
body: **Dustin 126.4, Andrew & Nick 29.6.** The 96.8-point margin is the season's biggest beatdown, and 29.6 is now the dud of the year. Andrew & Nick also left 30.2 points on the bench, which would not have come close.
Chris & Miguel ran Kevin over 142.4 to 67.2, and Michael beat Trey 120.7 to 63.8. Nathan took care of John 109.1 to 92.3 and now leads that series 13–5 all time.
The best game of the week was Mack edging Connor & Kunal 127.0 to 124.6. It was decided by 2.4 points and leaves that rivalry dead even at 8–8.

sections.head: Power shifts
body: Peyton and Chris & Miguel moved up a spot each. Connor & Kunal slid to No. 2 despite the league's best all-play mark. Dustin jumped three places to No. 9 on the strength of one enormous afternoon.
Mike slipped a spot to No. 4 at 4–4, though his last three weeks average 131.7, the best in the league. Trey is going the other way: 90.1 a week over the same stretch, and down to No. 8.

sections.head: The playoff picture
body: Connor & Kunal and Peyton are effectively in. Mack climbed from 88% to 98% with the win over Connor & Kunal, and Chris & Miguel went from 84% to 96%.

The loser of the week is Trey: a 70% playoff team a week ago, 41% today. That 28-point drop is the biggest in the league. Michael more than doubled his odds to 23%, and Dustin's 8% at 2–6 is at least a pulse.

sections.head: Game of the Week
body: Mike vs. Nathan. Mike is projected for 125.1, Nathan for 112.6, and Mike is a 65% favorite. The result moves the two teams' playoff odds by a combined 60 points. Mike sits at 80% in. Nathan, the league's unluckiest team, is at about one in three.
Also worth a look: Chris & Miguel are 65% favorites over the unbeaten Stools, projected 131.0 to 118.7. If 8–0 is going to become 8–1, that's the spot.

sections.head: Award watch
body: Connor & Kunal still own the top score of the year, 176.60 in Week 1, and lead the league in points with 1152.6. Peyton leads the waiver race thanks to Braelon Allen's 82.4 points as a starter. And Nathan's Week 2, when the best lineup on his own roster would have won, is still the bench blunder to beat at 44.1 points left on the pine.

groupme: 📰 Week 8 is in. Peyton is 8–0 but has scored like a 6.0-win team. Dustin beat Andrew & Nick by 96.8. Trey's playoff odds fell from 70% to 41%. And Mike vs. Nathan is the Game of the Week, with 60 points of playoff odds on the line.
